title: The ZIA provider's reorder registry: keys, locks and lifecycle across rule resources
aliases: concurrent map read and map write zia
cloud app control rule type reorder

checks.do: Whether an earlier create of the same resource type failed its post-POST read, when an apply hangs or a rule lands in the wrong place.
Whether the resource shares a registry key with a different resource or rule type, since the callbacks then judge rules they cannot list.
Which resource type registered first under a shared key, when a rule of another type does not take its order in a mixed apply.
Whether a rule deleted earlier in the run is still registered under its key.
Whether the rule's rank differs from its declared rank, which the worker reports on every pass without repairing.
Whether a create that posts at the staging order collides with an existing rule's order.
Whether the policy's order and rank match the declared values after an apply: re-read every rule in the policy rather than trusting the apply result.

registry-key-is-a-string.statement: All ZIA rule resources share one in-process registry, `rules`, whose entries are keyed only by a resource-type string chosen by the calling resource. A cycle's background worker is started by the first registration under a key, with that registration's `getCurrent` and `updateOrder` closures; a registration that finds the cycle open only adds its rule to the registry, and its own closures are never used.

quotes: // Reorder goroutine still running — just register, don't start another

upstream.note: Filing 2 (reorder redesign) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

done-channel-read-after-unlock.statement: At v4.8.3 the registration function releases the registry lock and only then reads the cycle's done channel from the shared `reorderDone` map. Concurrent registrations write that map under the lock, so the read is a data race against writes to any key and can abort the provider with "concurrent map read and map write"; it cannot return a different channel for the same key.

join-after-final-snapshot.statement: A registration decides whether to join a cycle with a non-blocking receive on the done channel under the registry lock. The channel is closed by the goroutine only after `reorderAll` has returned, and the worker's clean exit returns straight after a pass, without re-reading the registry under the lock. So a rule registered after the final pass took its registry snapshot, and before the channel closes, finds an open channel, starts no new worker, and is waited on by a cycle that never evaluated it.

create-registers-before-read-sites.statement: The same register, read, then mark order is in seven create paths: bandwidth control, CASB DLP, CASB malware, DLP web, endpoint DLP rules, NAT control and outbound email DLP. Each retries or returns on a failed read before it can mark the entry done. The other rule resources mark done immediately after registering.
create-registers-before-read-sites.conditions: Search at v4.8.3: for every zia/resource_zia_*.go, the line order of reorderWithBeforeReorder( or reorder(, HasError(), markOrderRuleAsDone( and waitForReorder( inside the Create function (git grep -nE with those patterns). Those seven have HasError() between register and mark; cloud app control, endpoint DLP sub-rules, file type, firewall DNS/filtering/IPS, forwarding control, sandbox, SSL inspection, traffic capture and URL filtering do not (18 resource files register in all). Files are unchanged at HEAD except cloud app control. The same seven creates also re-POST after a read error; see zia.terraform.error-handling:create-reposts-after-read-error-sites.

upstream.note: Filing 2 (reorder redesign) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

undone-entry-hangs-later-waiters.statement: So a create that fails its post-POST read leaves a registration that is never done. The next create or update of the same resource type, in the same provider process, registers into the still-open cycle, marks itself done, and blocks in `waitForReorder` on a cycle whose worker can never proceed. The re-POST on a failed read (see the error-handling subject) adds a further registration for each new ID. A failed read followed by a successful retry also hangs: the retry re-POSTs and registers a new ID under the same key while the first stays undone, so the create's own wait blocks.
undone-entry-hangs-later-waiters.conditions: Requires the first cycle's goroutine to still be running when the later resource registers (it does, since it cannot exit), both resources using the same registry key, and the failure persisting until the create timeout. Hang inferred from the code; not reproduced.

upstream.note: Filing 2 (reorder redesign) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

registry-entries-are-never-removed.statement: Registry entries are added on every create or update and never removed: not when a cycle finishes, not when the rule is deleted. A rule destroyed or replaced later in the same provider process stays registered under its key.

traffic-capture-joins-firewall-cycle.statement: So a traffic-capture create that runs while a firewall-filtering cycle is open joins that cycle: its rule is judged by the firewall callbacks, which never list it, and it is skipped. staging-order-never-reserved.statement: The staging seed is a package-level scalar set once per provider process and never changed by a create. Every later create of that resource in the process posts the same order; no resource reserves the next slot. Firewall filtering and traffic capture add one when they first compute the seed, and also never advance it.

create-retry-loses-declared-order.statement: In bandwidth control create the intended order is read from the request inside the retry loop, after the previous pass already replaced `req.Order` with the staging value. After an `INVALID_INPUT_ARGUMENT` retry, the order handed to the reorder engine is the staging order, not the one in the configuration. For cloud app control the rank is lost only when the declared rank is below 7.

rank-mismatch-never-repaired.statement: So when a registered bandwidth control or CASB DLP rule is at its declared order but not its declared rank, the worker reports a PUT each pass, no write happens, and the rank is never corrected. The pass is never clean; with the v4.8.3 worker nothing ends the cycle, and from v4.8.7 only the oscillation breaker does, abandoning the cycle with a WARN log and no error.
rank-mismatch-never-repaired.conditions: Requires the listed rank to differ from the declared rank while the order matches (rank is a configurable attribute on both resources; whether the API changes rank on its own was not tested), and no skipped rule in the cycle for the v4.8.7 breaker to fire.

oscillation-breaker-guard.statement: The v4.8.7 oscillation breaker counts a pass only when it issued PUTs, did not improve the at-target count, and had no skipped rules and no PUT errors. Any PUT still counts as progress for the no-progress counter, and for the skipped-rule give-up. The count applies only while the registration count is unchanged.

mixed-skip-write-path-is-unbounded.statement: So a cycle with one permanently skipped rule and another rule whose PUT succeeds but does not converge has no exit: the breaker needs no skipped rules, the no-progress counter resets on every PUT, the skipped give-up needs a pass with no PUT, and a clean pass needs no skipped rules. At v4.8.3 there is no breaker, and the same mixed state also never ends.
mixed-skip-write-path-is-unbounded.conditions: Requires, in one cycle, a registered rule that is never listed (stale entry, wrong-key or wrong-type registration, or a rule not yet visible) and a registered rule whose written order does not stick every pass. Reasoned from the quoted conditions; not run. The loop ends only when the process or Terraform's own timeout ends it.

upstream.note: Filing 2 (reorder redesign) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

oscillation-breaker-six-passes.statement: The reorder helper stops after six consecutive clean passes (`maxNonImprovingPutTicks = 6`), meaning passes that issue PUTs without improving the best at-target count and have no skipped rules and no PUT errors; a changed registration set, a skip or a PUT error resets the count, logs the contested rules and returns so the apply can complete; the provider comment says that without the breaker the cycle livelocks until Terraform's own context deadline.

rule-type-order-scope.title: Whether the API orders cloud app control, SaaS Security DLP and malware rules independently per rule type
rule-type-order-scope.blocks: stating whether a type-blind registry key actually mixes ordering ranges, or only mixes callbacks
rule-type-order-scope.detail: The provider scopes every list and get by a rule-type parameter, and its comment for cloud app control says each type has its own order sequence. No captured source states this for the SaaS Security DLP and malware rule APIs. Test in a scratch tenant by creating rules of two types and listing each type with the type parameter.

duplicate-order-on-create.title: What the ZIA API does with a create whose order equals an existing rule's order
duplicate-order-on-create.blocks: stating where a staged create lands and which neighbours move
duplicate-order-on-create.detail: The provider posts new rules at the highest existing order (or at a value reused by earlier creates). No captured source says whether the API rejects, inserts before, or renumbers around an equal order. Test by creating two rules at an existing order in a scratch tenant and listing every rule's order.
